title: Where's the metro?
title_target: სად არის მეტრო? — Sad aris met'ro?
goal: Ask for directions and understand the answer, name places around town, and use three endings that do the work of English place prepositions: -ში, -ზე, and -თან.
bekal: ask სად არის…? and understand the answer
give directions: right, left, straight on
name the important places in a city
ask people to repeat or to show you on a map

dialogs.title: დიალოგი — Lost on Rustaveli Avenue
dialogs.intro: Ani is looking for the metro station and asks a man at the bus stop. Georgian answers are usually long and full of hand gestures — notice how Ani asks for a repeat without any awkwardness.

lines.speaker: კაცი:
lines.id: The metro? It's right here, close by. Go straight.

lines.speaker: კაცი:
lines.id: Then right, by the pharmacy. The metro entrance is there.
lines.literal: then — to-the-right, pharmacy-at. metro's — entrance — there — is.

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Slowly, please.
lines.literal: sorry, couldn't — I-catch. slowly, if — possible.

lines.speaker: კაცი:
lines.id: Straight… a hundred meters… then right. Got it?

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: Yes, got it. Is it far?

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: And where's the bank? I need money.
lines.literal: and — where — is — bank? money — I-need.

lines.speaker: კაცი:
lines.id: The bank is by the metro, next to the hotel.

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: Thank you so much! You've been a great help.

notes: **Three endings that replace the place prepositions.** **-ში** = in (თბილის**ში** = in Tbilisi, სახლ**ში** = at home). **-ზე** = on / at (მაგიდა**ზე** = on the table, ქუჩა**ზე** = on the street). **-თან** = at / near / at someone's place (აფთიაქ**თან** = by the pharmacy, ექიმ**თან** = to the doctor's). A final -ი drops first, exactly as with -დან in unit 3.

⚠️ **Georgian doesn't distinguish "in" from "into", or "at" from "to".** *სახლში ვარ* = I'm at home; *სახლში მივდივარ* = I'm going home. Same ending; only the verb makes the difference. A big relief compared to German or Russian, which change the ending.

**ვერ, not არ.** Both mean "not", but **არ** = won't / doesn't, while **ვერ** = can't, beyond your ability. *არ გავიგე* means "I didn't catch it" (maybe you weren't listening); *ვერ გავიგე* means "I couldn't catch it" — and that's the right one when your Georgian isn't there yet. English uses "didn't" for both; Georgian doesn't.
**ვერ გავიგე — learn it as a whole.** It's the most useful sentence for your entire stay in Georgia. Its partners: *ნელა, თუ შეიძლება* (slowly, please) and *გაიმეორეთ, თუ შეიძლება* (please repeat).
**გასაგებია?** (gasagebia) — "got it?", and the answer is კი, გასაგებია. It often closes any explanation, from directions to lessons.
**ფეხით = on foot.** The -ით ending again, which you know from unit 5 — ფეხი (foot) → ფეხ**ით** (by foot). Unit 13 uses it for every kind of transport.
**მჭირდება = I need.** Another inverted verb: მჭირდება (I need), გჭირდება (you need), სჭირდება (he/she needs). It sounds heavy because of the ჭ inside; say m-ch'ir-de-ba slowly.

grammars.title: -ში, -ზე, -თან: which ending goes where
body: The rule makes sense once you think about the shape of the place.
after: ⚠️ Some places take **-ზე** even when English would say "in": ქუჩა**ზე** (in the street), ბაზრო**ბაზე** (at the bazaar), გაკვეთილ**ზე** (in class). If unsure, -ში is almost always safe for buildings and cities.
To say whose place someone is going to, use **-თან**: *ექიმთან მივდივარ* — I'm going to the doctor (literally "to the doctor's place").

grammars.title: Directions and position

head: Georgian
Say it
Meaning
rows: to the right, on the right
to the left, on the left

after: Notice that **მარჯვნივ** and **მარცხნივ** mean both "to the right" and "on the right" — once again, Georgian doesn't feel the need to separate movement from position here.

blocks.title: Six sentences for not getting lost
items: **როგორ მივიდე…?** (rogor mivide) — How do I get to…?
**ვერ გავიგე. ნელა, თუ შეიძლება.** — I didn't catch that. Slowly, please.
**რუკაზე მაჩვენებთ?** (rukaze machvenebt) — Can you show me on the map?

blocks.text: A practical note on asking for directions in Georgia: people almost never answer "I don't know". If someone isn't sure, they'll often point anyway so as not to disappoint you. So for any distance that matters, ask **two people**, and use big, clear landmarks — მეტრო, ეკლესია, მოედანი — rather than street names.

⚠️ The Tbilisi metro has two lines and bilingual signs, but the announcements inside the trains are in Georgian only. Two words that help: **შემდეგი სადგური** (shemdegi sadguri — next station) and **გასასვლელი** (gasasvleli — exit).

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

items: I didn't catch that. Please repeat.

answers: თბილისში — მაგიდაზე — აფთიაქთან — ბანკში — ქუჩაზე — ექიმთან
სად არის მეტრო? — პირდაპირ წადი. — ბანკი ახლოს არის. — ნელა, თუ შეიძლება. — ფული მჭირდება.
უკაცრავად, სად არის აფთიაქი? — პირდაპირ წადი, მერე მარჯვნივ. — შორია? — არა, ხუთი წუთი ფეხით. — ვერ გავიგე. გაიმეორეთ, თუ შეიძლება. — დავიკარგე.
